claim_tested: Fly Atossa acts through the DEAD-box protein Porthos
key_finding: Nuclear Atossa raises porthos mRNA and the mRNAs of LKR/SDH and GR/HPR; Porthos supports ribosome assembly and OxPhos. The link is transcript-level, with no co-IP between Atossa and Porthos reported.
context: Drosophila melanogaster, embryonic macrophages, germband invasion
confidence_and_limitations: Primary, strong in fly. Does not establish a physical complex, and nothing in human.

claim_tested: Porthos is an RNA helicase acting in ribosome biogenesis
key_finding: Aramis, Athos and Porthos are three DExD/H-box proteins governing ribosome biogenesis in Drosophila oogenesis; Porthos carries rRNA binding IDA and nucleolus IDA.
confidence_and_limitations: Primary. Constrains Porthos function to RNA, not DNA.

claim_tested: Which human DEAD-box helicase is the Porthos ortholog
key_finding: Fly pths/CG9253 (Q9VIF6) to human DDX47: 13/13 tools, best_score Yes, best_score_rev Yes, confidence high. Next candidate DDX49 at 2/13. Reverse DDX47 to pths 13/13, next Dbp45A 2/13.
confidence_and_limitations: Direct computed result. Reciprocal best hit satisfied in both directions.

claim_tested: Independent check of the Porthos-DDX47 assignment
key_finding: Q9VIF6 vs 58 human DEAD/DEAH-box proteins: DDX47 score 1643, 71.3% identity over 449 aa; next DDX49 960 (49.9%), margin 1.71x. Reverse Q9H0S4 vs 26 fly helicases: pths 1643, next Dbp45A 719, margin 2.29x.
confidence_and_limitations: Direct computed result, independent of DIOPT. Confirms a clean 1:1 assignment.

claim_tested: Does ATOSA contain a DNA-binding or chromatin-binding module
key_finding: ATOSA 1-230 (pLDDT 82.5) matches HORMA structures at TM 0.619-0.665 (ATG13 5XUY/5XV1/8DO8, S. pombe Mad2 4YK8, MAD2 2QYF/3GMH) at 7.8-10.7% identity. Disordered control 300-530 returns zero hits. DUF4210 module 870-1000 (pLDDT 84.2) tops out at TM 0.447 with no coherent fold family.
confidence_and_limitations: Direct computed result with a negative control. TM > 0.5 is the same-fold threshold.

citation: Foldseek TM-align vs AFDB/SwissProt, computed here
claim_tested: Which HORMA subfamily, and is this ATOSA-specific
key_finding: Top non-Atos hits all HORMA: MAD2 yeast 0.618, bacterial Cap7 0.602, MAD2 human 0.569, REV7 plant 0.567, HORMAD2 human 0.534, ATG101 0.493. Module conserved in ATOSA orthologs (mouse 93%, chicken 89.6%, Xenopus 82.6%, zebrafish 77-80%). Human ATOSB 1-230 is disordered (pLDDT 36.0), zero hits; its ordered 340-538 module matches the shared C-terminal Atos region at 13-14% identity.
context: Computational, AlphaFold models Q32MH5 and Q7L5A3
confidence_and_limitations: Direct computed result. The HORMA domain distinguishes ATOSA from ATOSB.

claim_tested: What biochemistry the HORMA fold predicts
key_finding: HORMA proteins wrap a C-terminal safety belt around short closure motifs in partners, forming topologically closed complexes.
context: S. cerevisiae Hop1, with Mad2 comparison
confidence_and_limitations: Primary, review-grade mechanism. Predicts protein-protein interaction, not nucleic acid binding.

key_finding: TRIP13 with p31comet engages the disordered HORMA N-terminus and unfolds it to release closure motifs.
context: Human and mouse, in vitro and spermatocytes
confidence_and_limitations: Primary. Supplies a discriminating assay for whether ATOSA behaves as a functional HORMA.

key_finding: InterPro assigns nothing to residues 1-462. Only IPR025261 (DUF4210) 878-936, IPR033473 1018-1075, PANTHER PTHR13199 463-1076.
confidence_and_limitations: The HORMA module is currently unannotated in InterPro, which is a gap, not a contradiction.

key_finding: 18 of the 23 IntAct records for Q32MH5 come from this one Y2H screen: KRT40, MAGEA6, MID2-2, SSX2IP, GOLGA2, TRIM27, CASS4-2, APC. MI score 0.56. No DDX or DHX protein.
confidence_and_limitations: Single method, no orthogonal confirmation. Sole source of the six GO:0005515 IPI annotations.

stance: refutes the human axis as currently evidenced
claim_tested: Does any DDX protein appear as an ATOSA partner
key_finding: IntAct: 23 records, all Y2H, no DDX/DHX, no AP-MS, no co-IP, no proximity labelling. STRING FAM214A: 14 partners all below combined score 0.52, text-mining driven; only UBE2H and HNRNPH1 carry an experimental subscore (0.457); no DEAD-box protein at any score.
confidence_and_limitations: Absence of evidence. BioGRID returned HTTP 401 without a registered key and BioPlex returned 404, so those two were not queried.

claim_tested: Are ATOSA and DDX47 co-expressed across human tissues
key_finding: Pearson on log2 median TPM across 54 tissues r = 0.713 (p = 1.4e-09), Spearman 0.679. That ranks 24th of 36 DEAD/DEAH-box genes (DDX46 0.869, DHX38 0.855, DDX42 0.836). ATOSB 0.165 (p = 0.23). DDX47 median TPM 0.00-1.99, at the quantification floor.
context: Human, 54 GTEx tissues, bulk median TPM
confidence_and_limitations: Direct computed result with a background panel. No specificity for DDX47; the DDX47 profile itself is unreliable at this expression level.

claim_tested: Do ATOSA and DDX47 occupy the same compartment
key_finding: FAM214A/ATOSA nucleoplasm; FAM214B/ATOSB nucleoplasm plus nucleoli fibrillar center; DDX47 nucleoli.
confidence_and_limitations: Antibody-based, database-level. A subnuclear mismatch, not a direct interaction test.

key_finding: Human ATOSA: six GO:0005515 protein binding (IPI, PMID 25416956) and GO:0005634 nucleus (ISS from Q7JXG9, plus IEA). Fly Atossa: GO:0005634 nucleus (EXP, PMID 35319107) only, no MF, no transcription BP. Mouse Atosa: ND for MF and BP.
confidence_and_limitations: GO holds no molecular function for Atossa in any species.

stance: refutes the human transcription claim as experimental
claim_tested: Is the human transcription-regulator statement experimentally grounded
key_finding: Human Q32MH5 FUNCTION carries ECO:0000250/UniProtKB:Q69ZK7; mouse Q69ZK7 carries ECO:0000269/PubMed:35319107. TAD1 24-32, TAD2 962-970 and the invasion region 878-935 in human are all ECO:0000250 from mouse. The DOMAIN comment is ECO:0000305 in fly and mouse.
confidence_and_limitations: The human claim is a two-step similarity transfer resting on one fly publication.

claim_tested: Is ATOSA a human transcription factor
key_finding: Neither FAM214A/ATOSA nor FAM214B/ATOSB appears anywhere in the 2765-row curated survey, which calls 1639 proteins TFs.
confidence_and_limitations: Expert-curated. A deliberate exclusion from the census, consistent with the absence of any DNA-binding fold.

citation: Motif scan of Q32MH5, computed here
claim_tested: Is there a zinc finger, AT-hook, HMG box, homeodomain or bZIP region
key_finding: None found across 1076 residues. No run of 4 or more consecutive basic residues. Cys 2.42%, net charge about +5. Only weak NLS-like KKNK at 532 and KRPK at 709, both inside disordered segments.
confidence_and_limitations: Direct computed result. Motif scans can miss unconventional DNA-binding surfaces.
